ads_ratio.reason: EDGAR per-share figures are per ordinary share and the Nasdaq price is per ADS; at a 1:1 ratio the two are identical, so no scaling changes any figure — the field exists so make_score does not refuse on DATA_GAP:ads_ratio
ads_ratio.source: Suzano Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024 (filed 2025-04-28), Note 1 (Company's operations): Suzano's ADRs, 'in a ratio of 1 (one) per common share', Level II, are traded on the NYSE under the ticker SUZ; corroborated by BNY Mellon depositary notices through April 2026 showing Ratio (Local Shares:DRs) 1:1

moat_against: Commodity price-taker: bleached eucalyptus kraft pulp price is set by the market (China demand, industry capacity additions); Suzano has no pricing power — gross margin ranged 32-50% over the last five fiscal years on price alone
Returns are cycle-determined, not franchise-determined: roic_proxy 17.7%/17.9% at the FY2021/22 price peak fell to 6.8% by FY2025 (fundamentals.json)
High leverage amplifies the cycle: net debt $14.54B (dcf_numbers.json), ~3.2x adjusted EBITDA in USD at FY2025 (company release) and several turns of the engine's normalized OE
BRL/USD exposure both ways: revenues are USD-linked but costs are in BRL, and USD debt/hedge marks produced a R$7.0B net loss in FY2024 on non-cash FX/derivative swings
New industry capacity (including Suzano's own Cerrado tonnes) pressures the very price it takes; environmental/land-use scrutiny of eucalyptus monoculture is a standing ESG overhang
moat_for: Structural cost advantage: own eucalyptus plantations with short harvest cycles close to the mills, integrated logistics and ports — pulp cash cost R$817/t in FY2025, lowest since 2021 (company FY2025 release)
Scale: world's largest hardwood pulp producer; Cerrado (Ribas do Rio Pardo) added 2.55Mt/yr (~20% more capacity, total ~13.4Mt market pulp) and cut consolidated pulp cash cost 6% in 2024 to R$828/t
Vertical integration into paper/paperboard/tissue and the 2024 US paperboard acquisition diversify the pulp-only exposure (market pulp still ~75% of FY2025 revenue per segments.json)
Through-cycle cash generation: OE positive 5/5 last fiscal years (dcf_numbers.json), including the 2023 pulp-price trough
moat_justification: World's largest hardwood pulp producer with a structural cost advantage — own fast-growing eucalyptus plantations, integrated logistics and the Cerrado mill (world's largest single pulp line, 2.55Mt, started Jul 2024) put it at the low end of the global cost curve (pulp cash cost R$817/t in FY2025, lowest since 2021) — but it is a pure price-taker in a commodity: no pricing power, gross margin swung 50.2% (FY2022) to 32.4% (FY2025) with the pulp cycle, and roic_proxy fell from 17.9% (FY2022) to 8.5% / 9.9% / 6.8% (FY2023/24/25), i.e. recent returns sit around, not well above, the cost of capital through this part of the cycle.
name: Suzano S.A.
one_liner: World's largest, lowest-cost hardwood pulp producer, moat 5/10 — Tier A by numbers on the normalized median base ($1.45/ADS): weighted IRR 21.2%, IV@15% $12.96 vs $8.50 price — but a levered commodity price-taker (net debt 8.1x normalized OE; bear case is Tier B at 16.4% IRR and the super-bear IV of $5.35 sits below the price), so size it like a B.

sbc_override.reason: DATA_GAP:sbc — SBC missing for fiscal years 2023, 2024, 2025 under the engine's AdjustmentsForSharebasedPayments tag (the filer stops tagging the cash-flow addback after FY2021; statements.json likewise finds only equity-statement / key-management share-based tags for those years). The value is 0.99x the last filed anchor, inside the 0.1x-10x estimate band, and is the maximum of the three gap years' compiled figures, so it errs conservative (more SBC = lower OE). SBC at this level is ~0.2% of revenue and ~1% of owner's earnings — immaterial to the verdict either way; the engine measures the exact impact in override_impact.
sbc_override.source: Anchor: last SBC value filed under the engine's tags is FY2021 R$99,740,000 (financials_history.csv: US$17,902,333 at the FY2021 period-end ECB rate 0.17949 in dcf_numbers.json fx_conversion). Cash-flow compilations of Suzano's own statements put share-based compensation at R$42.1M (FY2023) / R$99.1M (FY2024) / R$92.1M (FY2025); the override takes the highest of the three recent years. Declared in BRL, the reporting currency; the engine FX-converts at period-end rates.
